claims.text: The onset and progression of phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by impurity-induced Cu surface segregation.
Trace oxygen promotes diffusion of Cu atoms to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface-segregated Cu locally reduces the melting temperature.
The local melting-point reduction caused by Cu segregation triggers premelting and accelerates melting.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid and compositionally homogeneous, with a uniform elemental distribution.
Oxygen impurities disrupt the homogeneous FeNiCrCoCu lattice.
Oxygen-induced lattice disruption facilitates atomic diffusion.
Trace oxygen accelerates demixing in the alloy.
Cu is a lower-melting constituent of FeNiCrCoCu.
Cu-rich surface regions serve as nucleation sites for premelting and rapid phase transition during heating.
Oxygen-dosed nanoparticles will begin premelting at a lower temperature than the ultra-high-purity control.
Oxygen-dosed nanoparticles will progress to complete melting more rapidly than the ultra-high-purity control.
Oxygen-dosed nanoparticles will develop Cu-enriched surface layers detectable by compositional mapping.
The proposed mechanism is limited to the premelting-to-melting regime, approximately within 100°C of the alloy melting point.
An inert atmosphere will avoid extraneous oxidation so that controlled oxygen content remains the only experimental variable.
The oxygen concentration threshold required to produce significant surface segregation is unknown.
Other elemental diffusion processes may influence the thermal response of the complex alloy.
A lack of statistically significant earlier Cu segregation or lower premelting temperature after oxygen addition would falsify the proposed mechanism.
